  "summary": "Fixes out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities in UniValue's JSON tokenizer by enforcing the input buffer's end pointer during keyword and number parsing. Also updates the UniValue unit tests and fuzz target to exercise non-null-terminated input views.",

If an input slice ends abruptly on one of these tokens, the parser can read past the end pointer.",

result.summary: Fixes out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities in UniValue's JSON tokenizer by enforcing the input buffer's end pointer during keyword and number parsing. Specifically, replaces `strncmp` on keywords with length-aware string prefix checks and verifies bounds before reading adjacent digits in number prefixes. Also updates the UniValue unit tests and fuzz target to exercise non-null-terminated input views.
result.problem: UniValue's tokenizer accepts an explicit end pointer (allowing string views or slices without null terminators), but `getJsonToken()` assumed null-terminated input when matching keywords (`null`, `true`, `false`) with `strncmp` and when inspecting `firstDigit[1]` for leading zeros. If an input slice ends abruptly on one of these tokens, the parser can read past the end pointer.
evidence: Fixes #28260: 'getJsonToken assumes underlying string is null-terminated but requires end pointer'
result.scope_notes: Touches the subtree-like UniValue parser code under `src/univalue/` along with test fixtures.
result.card: Ensures UniValue's JSON tokenizer respects the input buffer end pointer rather than assuming null-terminated strings. In existing code, keyword checks via strncmp and number validation via firstDigit[1] could read past the end pointer when parsing string slices. This fixes issue #28260 and updates the fuzz test and unit test suite to test non-null-terminated input views.
